User authorizes continuing T3 research for disruptive classical factoring complexity reductions. No new improvement verified. Own research/findings/H011-coupled-inverse.md and adjacent H011-inverse-* scratch files only. No shared code/Lean/STATE edits, packages, delegation, publication, scheduling or commits.

This is a NEW revised research round, with original context and prior objections:
1. W001-lifting.md Card1 proposed inverse Taylor patches p=a+R*t modulo B=R^6, R=2^s, degree5. If total tree nodes were R*poly(log R), deterministic N^(1/6) cost might become possible.
2. H005 weak degree2 finite screen was inconclusive because intervals had at most2 integers.
3. H006 protocol/result remained inconclusive under its finite threshold. H006-independent-review.md (read FULL) now derives a uniform Theta(R^3) exhaustive exact-relaxation tree obstruction. Independent high-power tangent/secant boxes can choose z3,z4,z5 to solve arbitrary high digits. It supplies sound certificates, nested reachability, uniform elementary Kloosterman counting and actual clipped boxes. More supporting tangents cannot remove this freedom. It is NOT an early-stop lower bound or a general factoring lower bound. The parent checked the new derivation and is closing this full-tree route.
4. Simply imposing z_j=t^j as nonlinear constraints is not free fixed-dimensional linear integer programming. No oracle or hidden bits allowed.

New H011 question: can exact cross-power coupling be replaced by a COSTED modular-inverse interval-reporting algorithm with a smaller total bound? Here is one precise target, not an assumed primitive. For public R=2^s, odd N of size Theta(R^6), M=R^5, enumerate all odd p,q in the public intervals I,J subset [R^3/2,R^3), or precisely specified clipped Card1 intervals, satisfying p*q=N (mod M). Retain the actual factors by checking p*q=N. Because every product is <R^6, p*q=(N mod M)+k M for only O(R) nonnegative k. A trivial divisor bound gives at most R^(1+o(1)) output pairs for N=Theta(R^6), but obtaining them by factoring those O(R) integers is circular/expensive. This small OUTPUT bound is not an output-sensitive ALGORITHM.

Try ONE explicit construction: a continued-fraction/lattice decomposition of the modular inverse graph in boxes, or exact binary lifting with a genuinely coupled low-dimensional state. Specify the actual transition/query and all arithmetic work; identify a useful threshold if the R^1 target is too strong. To beat deterministic N^(1/5), total exponent in R must be below6/5, including any patches, base case factoring, point reporting and all boxes. Even that would remain slower asymptotically than heuristic GNFS, and balanced-box coverage alone is not an all-input algorithm.
Known low-bit Coppersmith thresholds and existing modular-hyperbola/lattice algorithms must be checked from primary sources rather than relabeled. No supplied factors, inverse-interval oracle, arbitrary nonlinear IP oracle, precomputed table or free factorization of shifted integers. Ordinary polynomial-time inverses modulo powers of2 are allowed; querying all p costs R^3 and is not a gain.

The concrete deliverable is an algorithm with complete cost analysis, or a precise failure/obstruction for the selected construction and an honest remaining bottleneck. Before any finite run freeze exact parameters, metrics, rejection criterion and <=60-second cap; preserve all generated/failed/unstarted cases and source/protocol hashes. A tiny success or few outputs does not show fast reporting. If no plausible executable transition exists, do not run a generic benchmark or broaden into a survey. No claimed polynomial factoring without a complete proof and later independent review. Do not duplicate the H010 circuit-width work or H008 resultant review.
